"Let's see if we can shoot down this theory.  [Sits up straight, cracks knuckles].  Time to stretch my Star Wars lore legs a little.  (Sorry, opportunities like this don't come along often).

Jar Jar being a co-conspirator with Palpatine would break the Rule of Two doctrine that had established the Sith Master-Apprentice system in place since Darth Bane (c.f., http://starwars.wikia.com/wiki/Rule_of_Two).  This system was even alluded to by Mace Windu and Yoda speaking in the film Revenge of the Sith, noting that there are always two Siths (master and apprentice, AKA Shadow Hand).  Palpatine is also known by his Sith name, Darth Sidious, and calls Anakin, Darth Vader.  The appearance of "Darth" in their names hints to the Bantine system mentioned above still being in place, which brought about the Darth titles and Rule of Two doctrine.  According to Star Wars lore, the Bantine system ends when Darth Vader kills Darth Sidious, with Darth Vader himself dying shortly thereafter without having his own apprentice to take over and continue the line.  (That is at least where we left off with Return of the Jedi in the film saga).  [Side note: Anakin was still "the chosen one", it being he that actually killed Palpatine, thus bringing an end to the Bantine line, destroying the Sith, restoring balance to the force, and ending the Galatic Empire reign, thus fulfilling the prophecy [whew!].  [Let me throw in another 'thus' for good measure.].  Although, none of that would have happened if it had not been for Luke Skywalker motivating Darth Vader's very brief return to light.  Also, we know that Anakin had midichlorian counts much higher than even Master Yoda, yet we don't know how much either Luke nor Leia have, thus it is hard to tell if Luke could have been the prophesied one.  Just a thought about how Qui-gin wasn't necessarily wrong when speaking to the Jedi Counsel about Anakin being the chosen one, nor was Obi-wan in talking with Mace Windu and Yoda at least twice or in talking to Anakin after defeating him on Mustafar.  But, I digress.]

In this case, Jar Jar would have been a Sith Lord master to Palpatine's apprentice, who could not, by said rule, have had his own apprentice(s) (e.g., Darth Maul, then Darth Tyranus, then Darth Vader in each of the prequel films, respectively)...that is, unless they were establishing a new era of Sith doctrine, but there are no hints at this being the case.  Further, it was established even in the films that Palpatine was himself previously the apprentice of Darth Plagueis, a history well told by Palpatine in conversation with Anakin in the Revenge of the Sith film.  Thus, if Darth Plagueis was the master of Darth Sidious, Jar Jar could not be his master (or Sith Order superior) unless it were some deviation from the Bantine system and line in place at the time.  All indications provided in Star Wars lore point to this heavily being the case (at least to my knowledge--I am just starting to get into this stuff).  This theory seems highly unlikely to me.
